newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- To stem losses from flights across the Atlantic, Trans World Airlines said on Monday it would cut some routes and possibly hundreds of jobs at its Kennedy International Airport hub.
- Mercantile Bancorporation Inc said on Monday it would acquire a rival, Roosevelt Financial Group Inc, for $1.07 billion.

- When real estate developers and retailers opened the Polus Center, the first American-styled shopping mall in Central Europe, they knew thay had to transplant the authentic ambiance of an American mall.
- After two exceptional years for stocks, investors are looking closely to see whether the strength in corporate earnings can continue.
- Americans' incomes and spending both increased in November.
- American General said it would buy Home Beneficial for $665 million.
- Archer Daniels Midland said it would buy the cocoa business of W.R. Grace for about $430 million in cash and debt.

- Teva Pharmaceutical of Israel received marketing clearance from the FDA for Copaxone to treat multiple sclerosis and Agouron Pharmaceuticals filed a request with the agency for permission to market Viracept to treat HIV.
- Prices of Treasury securities gained after the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for December fell.
- Dean Witter, Discover said it had agreed to buy Lombard Brokerage, a securities firm that offers trading via the Internet and a toll-free phone number.
- Tiffany and Co is advertising on television for the first time, in a tricky attempt to expand its consumer appeal without compromising its image.
- Genelink, a new company, promises to protect and preserve DNA, the material that contains people's genetic codes, in case it might be useful to future generations.
